problem: VLN suffers from data scarcity (Matterport3D has only 90 scenes). Prior augmentation such as PanoGen generates panoramas from text with Stable Diffusion but ignores 3D geometry, so the panoramas and trajectories are world-inconsistent and confuse the agent.
motivation: Poor generalization to unseen environments comes from limited environment diversity. Augmented data must be both diverse and spatially coherent, at the trajectory level (across viewpoints) and at the viewpoint level (seamless wraparound panorama). The authors argue that injecting camera projective geometry into diffusion generation can supply this consistency.
key_idea: Generate new VLN panoramas in two stages, with point-cloud reprojection across viewpoints and spherical angle-warp outpainting within a panorama, both feeding depth-conditioned ControlNet, then regenerate instructions with a fine-tuned video-captioning model.
insight: Geometry-guided warping and depth conditioning are what give the data its value. Removing viewpoint-stage outpainting (generating perspectives independently) drops R2R val-unseen SPL from 65.8 to 63.1, removing depth drops it to 62.8, and removing trajectory-stage temporal replenishment drops it to 64.9. Regenerated instructions add SPL 62.5 -> 65.8 over the original R2R instructions. Augmented data helps more in fine-tuning than in pre-training (SPL drops 5.9 vs 3.5 when omitted), and performance keeps rising past the size of the original R2R trajectory set.
method: Trajectory stage / Temporal Replenishment Module (TRM): for each viewpoint t, estimate depth of the previous reference image with a transformer depth estimator, back-project to a point cloud, transform with the inter-viewpoint pose, and re-project to get a guidance image G_t.

Reference image generation: ControlNet (depth) does image-to-image on the fragmentary G_t plus depth with reduced noise strength, giving the reference image Y_t. If there is no overlap, or at t=1, it falls back to text-to-image conditioned on depth, or the original image.
Viewpoint stage / Spatial Outpainting Module (SOM): outpaint the remaining perspective images of a panorama progressively, in a target-queue order that circles the panorama from the reference image.

Novel angle synthesis: warp each neighboring generated view onto the target view via unit-sphere rotation, giving a guidance image and mask; the mask edges are blurred; multiple neighbors are combined by a weighted sum; ControlNet outpaints with depth and mask.
LLM prompts: GPT-4 extracts a coarse layout description and fine-grained object information from each real view as text prompts for the diffusion model.
Instruction generation: fine-tune mPLUG-2 (video captioning) on the Matterport3D training set to write instructions for the generated trajectories.
Agent training: DUET is pre-trained and fine-tuned with the augmented environments, using CLIP ViT-B/16 features.

setting.backbone: DUET (trained with augmented data); generation uses ControlNet-depth, SDXL, GPT-4, mPLUG-2, CLIP ViT-B/16
setting.training_data: R2R/R4R/REVERIE/CVDN training data plus WCGEN-synthesized panoramas and instructions (5000 trajectories in the best R2R setting; 4,676 is the R2R training trajectory count)
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth, camera parameters and poses are used only during data generation on training scenes)

results: WCGEN+DUET reaches R2R val-unseen SR 75.0 / SPL 65.8 and R2R test SPL 64.5, beating PanoGen (SPL 64.3 / 63.9) and the DUET baseline (SPL 60.0 / 59.0). It also gains on R4R (SPL 45.3 vs PanoGen 44.3) and on CVDN (GP 6.47 vs PanoGen 5.93 on val-unseen). On REVERIE, OSR and SPL improve but RGSPL is slightly below DUET (22.33 vs 22.89).
limitations: Small target objects, such as candles, are handled poorly, giving RGSPL below DUET on REVERIE.
The generation pipeline is heavy (depth estimation, ControlNet, GPT-4, mPLUG-2), and gains over PanoGen are modest, roughly 0.6-1.5 SPL.
Only DUET is evaluated as the agent, and extra-simulator data methods are excluded from the comparison.
